newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy satisfied with lira re-entry in ERM.
newsitem.headline: Italy satisfied with lira re-entry in ERM.

text.p: Italy was satisfied on Monday with its re-entry into the Exchange Rate Mechanism after four years of absence, even though it failed to return at an exchange rate it initially wanted.

After two days of tough bargaining it had to accept that a European Union majority wanted the lira to enter the currency grid at a stronger rate than the 1,000 lire per mark it sought. The eventual entry rate was 990 lire per mark.
"We were aiming for a 1,000 lire per mark, but I am satisfied with the (agreed) parity," Treasury Minister Carlo Ciampi told reporters.
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said the agreed rate seemed to be well balanced.
"The new parity is close to equilibrium," he said.
In Rome, Prime Minister Romano Prodi hailed the deal as a firm step towards Italy's goal of becoming the founding member of a joint currency in 1999.
"This result represents a premise for the lowering of the cost of money and constitutes a fundamental step for our participation in the monetary union," he was quoted as saying.

Ciampi and Fazio also said that by letting the lira return to the ERM, other European states acknowledged a "substantial adjustment" achieved by Italy's economy. They both renewed a pledge to maintain prudent policies and stable currency.

"(There is) an explicit indication of the will to pursue a monetary and fiscal policy coherent with a 990 lire to the mark level," Fazio said, adding that level was sustainable and even left room for the lira's appreciation.
He said the exchange rate would have no implications for the interest rate policy, which is influenced chiefly by inflation developments, which he termed as favourable.
The Italian officials also said that the differences on the parity rate resulted partly from earlier actions by the Bank of Italy to shore up other currencies in preparations for the ERM entry.
They said this was interpreted by EU partners as an attempt to steer the lira's market rate to a level more favourable for Italy.
